newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait to sell Real Estate Bank shares.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait to sell Real Estate Bank shares.

text.p: Kuwait plans to sell 60 million shares of the about 70 million Kuwait Real Estate Bank (KREB) shares it holds to private subscribers, the Kuwaiti news agency Kuna reported on Sunday. "The Kuwait Investment Authority
(KIA) announced today (Sunday) that it will put 60 million state-owned KREB shares for public subscription," said the agency.
KIA has set the offer price at 350 fils per share, said the agency. The KREB share, which fetched a 435 fils in the auction, closed at 365 on Sunday. There are 1,000 fils to the dinar.
The sell off is the second phase of a KREB privatisation bid by KIA, the state investment arm, which sold another 30 million shares in a November auction.
The state's initial stake in KREB stood at 32.9 percent of its issued shares.
KIA has named Securities Group as manager and underwriter for the sale, said the agency.

KREB, which chiefly extends medium- and long-term loans to construction projects and poperty investment, had reported a 101.8 percent rise in the first half of 1996 compared with the same period in 1995, rising to 3.5 million dinars.

The sale is part of Kuwait's plan to shed state holdings in about 60 local firms and public services such as electricity, water and telecommunications. The plan, announced after the 1991 Gulf War, is under the supervision of KIA.
Only nationals of Kuwait and fellow Gulf Arab states -- Saudi Arabia, Oman, Qatar, Bahrain and the United Arab Emirates -- can trade shares of local firms.
